basis: Inherited retinal degeneration; sino-oto-pulmonary manifestations are not established as common across RPGR retinopathies.
Organic aciduria with developmental impairment and neutropenia; cataracts in 80-99%. Renal cysts/nephrocalcinosis also 80-99%, omitted under cap.
Adenoma arising in the parathyroid endocrine gland.
Congenital loss of intestinal ganglion cells causes persistent colonic dysmotility and obstruction; no generalized neurologic disease implied.
Chronic sinobronchial disease defines the syndrome; recurrent middle-ear inflammation occurs in 30-79%. Reproductive obstruction has no axis.
Benign endometrial stromal neoplasm confined to the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no axis.
Corneal epithelial loss and inflammation; the umbrella includes infectious and noninfectious ulcers.
Parathyroid hormone excess; skeletal demineralization affects roughly 30% or more across typical forms. Renal failure is often a cause, and stones a separate disease.
Chorioretinal lesions directly cause atrophic scars, neovascularization and subretinal fibrosis; no extraocular disease established.
Structural malformation of the thyroid endocrine gland.
Testicular germ-cell tumour; reproductive origin without a defining endocrine disorder has no axis.
Disease located in tendons, which belong to the locomotor system.
Autoinflammatory mevalonate kinase deficiency; oral ulcers ~60%, gut bleeding 80-99%, arthritis ~67%. Vasculitis 30-79% omitted under cap; rash is transient.
Epilepsy triggered by visual stimuli; the trigger does not imply eye damage.
Lobular epithelial proliferation of the breast; breast disease has no axis despite the broad integumentary parent.
Skeletal-muscle channelopathy with obligatory episodic hypokalemia; arrhythmia and respiratory complications are below 30%.
Malignancy occupying the lacrimal drainage system, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Persistent congenital arterial connection; pulmonary arterial involvement remains cardiovascular, without intrinsic lung damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with neuropathy, leukoencephalopathy and gut dysmotility; ophthalmoplegia 80-99%. Myopathy and hearing loss 30-79% omitted under cap.
Inherited susceptibility specifically targets colorectal neoplasia; this label identifies the target organ without assuming an existing tumour.
Congenital splenoportal venous abnormalities; hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis and encephalopathy are reported without frequencies establishing the 30% threshold.
Transplacentally acquired autoimmunity; affected organs vary among neonatal autoimmune subtypes, with no additional organ established across most cases.
Microcornea, retinal dystrophy, cataracts and posterior staphyloma define an exclusively ocular syndrome.
Joubert syndrome is defined by cerebellar-brainstem malformation and neurodevelopmental dysfunction; no subtype-specific evidence supports additional organs.
Nephrotic disease and CNS anomalies define the syndrome; developmental hiatus hernia occurs in 30-79%. External-ear dysmorphism does not establish functional ear damage.
